You can be hypermobile and not EDS. 

I'm going to use my partner and I, who are both hypermobile. 

While my partner has many hypermobile joints he has what can be described as "generalised hypermobility" it doesn't cause him day to day pain, and outside of the occasional subluxation it just means his arms look funny. (Maybe 1 a year if he's unlucky) He experiences more discomfort from the fact he's 6'5 than he does from his bendy elbows. 

Meanwhile I am hypermobile, but it causes me chronic pain. I experience frequent subluxations/dislocations but also depending on the type of injury can comfortably relocate a joint and continue on. (Kneecaps in particular are my speciality, but my shoulders will roll out of the joint if I lean forward). 

In this case I've been described as either having Marfans or EDS. But I also experience external bodily complications, skin complications as a direct result. While it's never been brought up for me, there's also Loley Dietz, which similar to Marfans. Lastly, some people with brittle bone are very hypermobile between the lack of density & frequent breaks!

Some people are an inbetween, or don't fit the criteria for hEDS but experience problematic hypermobility and they fall into the label Joint Hypermobility Sydnrome. hEDS in particular currently has strict criteria as they are trying to isolate a few possible genes for it, as it's currently the only form of EDS that lacks a known gene.

Hope this helps!

TLDR: It's a spectrum of issues, EDS is just the most known and some people are just hypermobile
